Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Leah Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Meridian CTO), Ethan Liu (Meridian ML Eng), Priya Rao (Product), Carlos Mendez (Infra)

Summary (auto): Initial discovery to understand migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated and validate compatibility with current tooling (vLLM/TGI), discuss performance and security constraints, and agree pilot scope.

Transcript:
[00:00] Leah: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Leah, I'm the AE on this account, I'll run the intro. Samir is our solutions engineer, he'll hop into the deep technical bits.
[00:10] Aisha: Hey Leah, hi Samir, thanks. Quick context: Meridian runs customer-facing summarization and chat features through OpenAI, about 200M tokens a month, spikes to 5k rps during business hours, and we're seeing some latency and cost surprises.
[00:25] Samir: Cool, thanks Aisha. Can you say more about the latency profile? tail vs median?
[00:33] Ethan: Yeah so median's fine, like 150-200ms for short prompts, but the tail climbs — 800ms to 1.2s on longer threads. And cost, we feel like as we scale it's getting expensive, plus we want more deterministic SLAs.
[00:48] Priya: Also interested in eval parity. We run internal evals against OpenAI and need to avoid regressions when switching models.
[00:58] Leah: Totally — that's exactly why people look at Redwood Dedicated: predictable throughput and the ability to pin model versions plus tooling to run evals. Quick agenda: current stack, compatibility with vLLM/TGI, perf and cost, security, pilot scope. Cool?
[01:12] Aisha: Yes.
[01:15] Samir: Quick clarification — when you say you use vLLM, do you have a TGI wrapper or a custom serving layer?
[01:23] Ethan: We have a hybrid. We started with TGI locally for experiments then moved to vLLM for production for a few endpoints. We did some custom KV cache experiments.
[01:31] Samir: That helps. On Redwood Dedicated we support the model variants you likely run, and we have migration paths for both TGI and vLLM workloads. There are some differences in tokenization edge cases and sampling defaults, so we usually do an eval parity pass.
[01:46] Aisha: Sampling defaults — can you be more specific? We noticed subtle changes in temperature responses when we tried a community quantized model.
[01:53] Samir: Yeah, quantization + kernel selection can change output distributions a bit. We have a recommended quantization profile and sequence-length aware kernels; we also recommend running the same prompt set through both stacks and doing a delta analysis.
[02:07] Ethan: For the delta analysis, do you ship any tooling or is that on us?
[02:12] Samir: We provide a benchmarking harness — I'll share a small runner and a spreadsheet template. It automates request replay, collects latency histograms, token counts, and simple quality metrics.
[02:21] Priya: Great. For security, we need to ensure SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. Also important: data residency for EU customers.
[02:30] Leah: On security: Dedicated supports customer VPCs, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and we can do SAML SSO. We have SOC2 and ISO material — I'll send the pack. If you need on-prem, we have a private deployment option as well.
[02:43] Carlos: For on-prem, is it the same control plane or fully air-gapped? We have some regulated clients that demand air gap.
[02:51] Samir: We offer both a customer-managed control plane and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments — there are tradeoffs on telemetry but it's a supported path.
[03:02] Aisha: Can you give an example of expected latency at ~5k rps on Dedicated?
[03:07] Samir: It depends on model and GPU. For a Llama 2 13B-ish style model on 8xA100-equivalent pools with batching tuned, you'd typically see medians in the 100-200ms range for short prompts and tail under 400-500ms with proper KV cache. But the numbers vary with quantization and sequence length.
[03:27] Ethan: How does Redwood handle KV cache? Our current vLLM setup pins big context windows but we've seen cache invalidation issues at scale.
[03:35] Samir: Redwood runtime does continuous batching and KV cache management; we do proactive eviction and hot-key routing so your hot sessions get pinned to same workers, reducing cache misses. Transcription note: I said K-V cash earlier, sorry.
[03:48] Leah: Do you have strict uptime SLOs you need?
[03:51] Aisha: We aim for 99.9% for customer-facing features, and we'd like a predictable burst policy for Black Friday-like events.
[03:59] Leah: Dedicated has SLA options and configurable autoscaling with burst pools. For burst capacity we can reserve a baseline and allow bursts with upfront burst credits in contract.
[04:12] Priya: About cost — what's the ballpark delta compared to OpenAI for our workloads? We're paying per-token now, want to see unit economics improvements.
[04:20] Samir: It depends on utilization. With Dedicated reserved capacity, your per-token cost can drop substantially because of amortized GPU costs and local KV caching, especially for repeated prefixes. I'll put some calc examples in the pricing doc.
[04:31] Ethan: Are there any gotchas moving from OpenAI response formats/functions? We use function calling heavily.
[04:37] Samir: Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output. We map OpenAI-style function calls to our interface; you may need a small adapter layer if you rely on very vendor-specific behaviors.
[04:49] Aisha: Eval parity — we've got a 2-week A/B evaluation where we compare OpenAI against baseline. What do you suggest we run for parity checks?
[04:57] Samir: Run your exact prompt set and collect: automatic metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/embeddings cosine) and human spot checks for critical flows. We'll help you set up the runner and share the spreadsheet template. Also check for tokenization differences — sometimes punctuation or truncated tokens change model outputs.
[05:15] Priya: Do you support model pinning and gradual rollouts? We want canary and fallback to OpenAI if something is off.
[05:21] Leah: Yes, Redwood has rollout policies: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to another model or region. You can pin versions per route.
[05:29] Carlos: On the infra side — how would networking look? VPC peering vs private link?
[05:34] Samir: We support VPC peering, private link options, and customer-managed NAT — for Dedicated we can co-locate in your VPC. For private/on-prem it's different but doable.
[05:44] Ethan: Any differences when running community quantized models vs vendor models?
[05:49] Samir: Quantized models can have slightly different floating point behavior; our runtime picks quantization-friendly kernels, but we strongly recommend a parity run. Also, if you use TGI runtime, watch for tokenization and sampling default differences.
[05:59] Aisha: Timeline wise we'd like to decide within 4 weeks — procurement and security review will take another 2. So ideally a pilot within next 2 weeks.
[06:09] Leah: That's reasonable. Proposed pilot: 2-week benchmark on a small Dedicated pool (2 GPU nodes), run your prompt set, parity vs OpenAI, and a cost analysis. If that looks good we can scale to reserved capacity discussions.
[06:22] Priya: What's the minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[06:24] Leah: We have monthly reserved capacity and annual committed tiers. For pilots it's flexible, we can do month-to-month eval pricing and then convert to reserved. I'll include examples.
[06:34] Ethan: Regarding tooling — will your harness allow replaying OpenAI traffic including rate limits and backpressure simulation?
[06:40] Samir: Yes, the harness supports replay with configurable concurrency and simulated backpressure. We'll provide the commands and a Docker image.
[06:49] [Speaker 1]: um yeah, so uh, can we also log all requests locally for compliance?
[06:54] Leah: For audit logs we can stream them into your S3 bucket or to your SIEM depending on the deployment.
[06:59] Aisha: Any references to previous migrations you can point to? Case studies?
[07:03] Leah: We'll send a short case study on a fintech customer who moved from OpenAI to Dedicated and saw 40% lower per-token cost and improved latency.
[07:12] Ethan: For the parity tests, do you support temperature/seed control to reduce nondeterminism?
[07:18] Samir: We support deterministic sampling and seeded generation where the model family allows it. We'll document the supported knobs per model.
[07:26] Priya: Data retention and deletion policies? We need to prove we can delete customer data on demand.
[07:31] Leah: Dedicated gives you control — we can configure retention windows and have deletion workflows, and for Private you control data lifecycle entirely.
[07:39] Carlos: Any SOC2 / ISO timelines if we need extra attestations?
[07:43] Leah: Redwood maintains SOC2 and ISO docs; if you need an additional attestation we can discuss but usually the standard pack suffices.
[07:50] Aisha: Ok, let's talk about compatibility with our vLLM tuning. We have custom LoRA adapters and some prompt-tuning. Will those transfer?
[07:59] Samir: You can bring LoRA/adapters into Redwood, but we validate adapter compatibility during onboarding. For some quantized paths you might need to re-export the adapter. We'll help with that during the pilot.
[08:10] Ethan: What about embedding workflows? We use OpenAI embeddings for search ranking.
[08:15] Leah: We support embeddings generation and have a model catalog. If you want to move embeddings in-house for cost reasons we can run a small benchmark to validate vector quality and recall.
[08:26] Priya: Can your runtime do on-the-fly reranking or do we need a separate service?
[08:31] Samir: You can do reranking as part of the pipeline — Redwood supports both generation and embedding routes; many customers run rerankers on the same cluster.
[08:38] Aisha: Let's surface blockers: 1) we need eval parity assurance, 2) procurement and SOC2 check, 3) cost projections.
[08:46] Leah: Agree. We'll action those: pricing, security docs, and the benchmarking harness.
[08:51] Ethan: For the bench, can we include variable sequence lengths and multi-turn histories? That's often where tails spike.
[08:58] Samir: Absolutely. The harness supports multi-turn replay with configurable memory windows to simulate real sessions.
[09:05] Priya: Any latency guarantees for on-prem vs Dedicated hosted?
[09:09] Leah: On-prem gives you full control but comes with operational overhead. Dedicated hosted gives SLAs and Redwood-managed infra; both can meet low-latency needs with proper sizing.
[09:19] Aisha: One more security Q: who has access to logs in the Dedicated control plane? We need RBAC and audit trails.
[09:27] Samir: We have RBAC, role-level permissions, and audit logs. For Dedicated you can also configure which Redwood engineers get access (least privilege).
[09:36] [00:09:40] Leah: Quick recap — Redwood to send pricing and security pack, Samir to share harness and spreadsheet, Meridian to share traffic samples and prompt set. Pilot scoped to 2 weeks on 2 GPUs.
[09:48] Aisha: Sounds good. I'd like to get Samir and Ethan to do a technical deep dive next week focused on adapter export and tokenization diffs.
[09:56] Samir: Happy to — let's pick a slot.
[10:00] Leah: I'll send calendar invite. Any other questions?
[10:04] Priya: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[10:07] Aisha: Thanks.
[10:09] Leah: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs.

(Transcript ends — approximate timestamps every section; auto-transcription contains minor misattributions and occasional filler words.)
